title: Impossibility of perfect-completeness testing
statement: Let $\alpha<1$. There do not exist an error function $\lambda:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and a family of randomized finite-query testers, one for each positive dimension, with all of the following properties: each tester uses only predicates that accept triples of signs exactly when their product equals a fixed sign; its predicate family is finite; and for some acceptance threshold $\beta=1$, one has $0<\alpha<\beta\le1$. The error values lie in $[0,1]$ for inputs in $[0,1]$ and tend to $0$ as the input decreases to $0$ through positive values. Every dictator (the function returning one chosen coordinate) is accepted with probability at least $\beta$, while every function whose stable influence at each coordinate is at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha+\lambda(\varepsilon)$, for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
